technical.summary: Strong trend structure with multiple moving average confirmations and ADX strength, but overbought conditions across RSI/Stoch/UO and bearish MACD crossover create pullback risk; moderate entry quality with elevated caution.

fundamental.summary: GE shows no actionable smart money signals with zero insider activity, no institutional positioning data, absent government contract wins, no lobbying activity, and minimal retail interest; earnings in 85 days adds timing risk.

sentiment.summary: Weak bearish congressional signal from small sales 179-228 days ago; neutral market sentiment with balanced fear/greed and AAII; insufficient data for conviction.

risk.summary: Severe macro headwinds: inverted yield curve signals recession risk, VIX at crisis levels (185.3) indicates extreme market stress, FOMC event in 2 days adds near-term volatility; GE as industrial cyclical faces significant downside risk despite falling DXY tailwind.

debate.key_bull_argument: Strong ADX trend structure with EMA 50/200 bullish alignment and PSAR confirmation provides technical foundation, but overbought conditions and bearish MACD crossover signal imminent pullback risk.
debate.key_bear_argument: Severe macro headwinds (inverted yield curve, VIX crisis levels at 185.3, FOMC event in 2 days), zero fundamental conviction, earnings risk in 85 days, and overbought technicals across RSI/Stoch/UO create a high-probability pullback scenario for a cyclical industrial stock.

decision.entry_rationale: Technical trend structure is intact with ADX strength and EMA alignment, but macro environment is severely hostile with inverted yield curve and VIX crisis levels creating unacceptable systemic risk for a cyclical industrial stock.
decision.primary_risk: Inverted yield curve + VIX at 185.3 + FOMC event in 2 days creates high probability of sharp pullback; GE as cyclical industrial will amplify downside in recession scenario.
decision.agent_agreement: strong — all agents aligned on bear case
decision.portfolio_note: Already holding GE position with 45 existing Industrials positions (11% of portfolio); concentration risk and sector saturation argue against adding exposure.
